Pushed `8fb027c` to fix the `golangci-lint` failure in the new test file:

- `require.True(t, errors.Is(err, ErrNoAuthSession), …)` → `require.ErrorIs` (testifylint `error-is-as`) and dropped the now-unused `errors` import
- added the blank line `wsl_v5` wanted before the `auth_id` assignment

**Lint, Tests, Build and every other workflow are now green.**

The only remaining red checks are two integration jobs that look like pre-existing flakes unrelated to this change (it only touches the SSH-check follow-up path in `hscontrol/noise.go`):

- **`TestAuthKeyLogoutAndReloginSameUser`** — full-mesh ping fails with `unknown peer` after relogin. Its sibling `TestAuthWebFlowLogoutAndReloginSameUser` failed on one of my runs and passed on the next, and `TestAuthKeyLogoutAndReloginSameUser` is currently failing on other branches too (e.g. the recent `kradalby/sadit` integration run).
- **`TestDERPVerifyEndpoint`** — fails while *building* the tailscale-HEAD `derper` container (`go install -v ./cmd/derper` exits 1), i.e. an environment/build hiccup rather than an assertion. It passes on other recent branches.

Could a maintainer re-run the two failed jobs when convenient? Happy to rebase if you'd prefer. Thanks!

Pushed `67b0ac1` — a root-cause fix for the `TestDERPVerifyEndpoint` failure, which turns out to be a current main-wide CI breakage rather than anything specific to this PR:

tailscale HEAD's `go.mod` now requires **Go 1.26.4**. Commit `8f75ee5` ("docker: head tailscale latest go") bumped `Dockerfile.tailscale-HEAD` to `golang:1.26.4-alpine` accordingly, but `Dockerfile.derper` was left on `golang:1.26.3-alpine`. So `go install ./cmd/derper` against tailscale HEAD now fails the Go-version check, and `TestDERPVerifyEndpoint` fails at the derper image build for every PR on current main.

Bumping `Dockerfile.derper` to `golang:1.26.4-alpine` to match its sibling fixes it — verified locally (the derper image now builds and the binary runs). Happy to split this into a standalone PR if you'd prefer to land the CI fix on its own.

The remaining `TestAuthKeyLogoutAndReloginSameUser` is the known relogin mesh-ping flake (it's failing on other branches too); a re-run of just that job should clear it.
Looks good, need some more tests and terser comments in the code. Test comments are fine.
Also want to say, thank you very much for help testing!

Thanks for the review! All addressed in `92bb5b4` (force-pushed — now a single commit):

1. **`noise.go` comment** — trimmed to explain the *why* (a missing session dead-ends the client: it keeps polling the now-defunct `auth_id` until the SSH connection times out) and dropped the issue link.
2. **CHANGELOG** — removed; the feature is unreleased, so it ships with the next release's changelog as you said.
3. **End-to-end tests** — the missing-session re-delegation and the no-check rejection now both go through the real `SSHActionHandler` with a policy-resolved SSH check (`autogroup:self` over a same-user pair), alongside the persisted-session happy path. Taking it all the way up through a tailscale client would need the docker integration suite as you noted — happy to add that there too if you'd like, just point me at the preferred spot. (Added a small `UpdatePolicyManagerNodesForTest` helper mirroring the existing `...UsersForTest` so the handler test can resolve the policy.)
4. **`Dockerfile.derper`** — dropped that commit; I'll let your fix land.

Updated in `fce2db2` per your feedback:

- **Real-client test** — `hscontrol/servertest/sshcheck_test.go` now drives the fix end to end: the dst node polls `/machine/ssh/action` over its real Noise connection (`controlclient.Direct`) with a dead `auth_id` and asserts the server re-delegates. This replaces the httptest handler test.
- **Relocation** — the unit-level cases moved into `noise_test.go`; the separate file and the temporary `state` test helper are gone.
- Happy to add a full `integration/` scenario on top if you'd like the live-client coverage too — just say the word.

Reworked the tests per your feedback — `69a6a4e`.

**Integration test** — `TestSSHCheckModeSessionLossReDelegates` reproduces the real bug with a real client: an SSH in check mode is pending a verdict when the control plane **restarts** (dropping the in-memory auth cache while the DB and keys persist). The client keeps polling the now-missing `auth_id`, the server re-delegates a fresh session, that check is approved, and the SSH completes. Verified locally end to end:

- **with the fix → PASS** — the client recovers and the SSH succeeds
- **fix reverted → FAIL** at `new auth-id not found` — no re-delegation, i.e. the #3305 hang

(Added `hsic.Restart()` for the control-plane restart, and a `doSSHCheckWithTimeout` so the SSH outlasts it.)

**servertest** — reworked to your suggestion: no fabricated `auth_id` anymore. The dst node's real control client does an initial poll to get a genuine `auth_id`, that session is then **removed from the cache** to reproduce a natural loss, and the follow-up must re-delegate.

`noise_test.go` keeps the unit-level edge cases (persisted happy path, no-check rejection).

Thanks for pushing on this — the restart-based integration test is a much better guard than what I had.
Thank you, this looks could, can you fix the last two failures? rebase from main as I merged my change, then fixup lint and you must regenerate the integration tests.

message:
noise: re-delegate SSH check when the auth session is missing

A follow-up SSH check poll (/machine/ssh/action/{src}/to/{dst}?auth_id=...)
returned 400 "no auth session found" whenever the auth session referenced by
the auth_id was no longer in the in-memory auth cache (expired, evicted from
the bounded LRU, or lost when the control plane restarted). The polling client
cannot recover from this on its own: it keeps retrying the same now-defunct
auth_id until the SSH connection times out with no shell.

When the (src, dst) pair is still subject to an SSH check, restart the flow by
issuing a fresh HoldAndDelegate instead of erroring, so the check can complete.
Bogus auth_ids for pairs not subject to a check are still rejected.

Tests:
- integration: TestSSHCheckModeSessionLossReDelegates SSHes in check mode with a
  real client, restarts the control plane (dropping the in-memory auth cache)
  while the SSH is pending, and asserts the client recovers via re-delegation
  and completes. Verified to fail without the fix (no new auth_id is minted).
  Adds hsic.Restart() for the control-plane restart.
- servertest: the dst node's real control client polls the action endpoint over
  Noise; the cached session is removed to reproduce a natural loss, and the
  follow-up must re-delegate (no fabricated auth_id).
- noise_test.go keeps the unit-level edge cases (persisted happy path and the
  no-check rejection).

Addresses #3305

The latest run is green except for 3 jobs, and they're the known relogin/mesh-ping flake — not anything this change touches:

- `TestAuthKeyLogoutAndReloginSameUser`
- `TestAuthWebFlowLogoutAndReloginSameUser`
- `TestAuthWebFlowLogoutAndReloginNewUser`

In that run, 2 of the 4 clients (the `head` and `unstable` builds) never converged their netmaps after relogin — every ping came back `unknown peer` (empty peer list) right through the retry window, while the other 2 clients were fine. That's the map-propagation convergence timing you're already reworking on `main` (the recent `mapper:` commits / the `flake` commit).

Everything this PR actually changes is green: `check-tests`, `golangci-lint`, `TestDERPVerifyEndpoint`, and the new `TestSSHCheckModeSessionLossReDelegates`. Could you re-run those 3 jobs when you get a chance? Thanks again!
